idea.body: An inscribed angle has its vertex on the circle, with its two sides as chords. It is always exactly half the arc it looks at, no matter where on the circle its vertex sits. A tangent-chord angle, where a tangent and a chord meet at the point of tangency, follows the same half-the-arc rule. Where two chords cross inside a circle, the angle is half the sum of the two arcs cut off on opposite sides. Where two secants, or a secant and a tangent, meet outside a circle, the angle is half the difference of the far and near arcs. A wheel's inscribed angle P looks at an arc AB of 80 degrees, so angle P is 40 degrees.

figure.alt: A circle with inscribed angle P looking at arc AB.

workedExample.prompt: In a circle, chords AC and BD cross inside it. Arc AB is 70 degrees and arc CD is 50 degrees. Find the angle at the crossing point.
steps: An angle formed by two chords crossing inside a circle is half the sum of the two arcs on opposite sides.
Take half of that sum: 120 divided by 2 is 60 degrees.
The angle at the crossing point is 60 degrees.

ways.name: Inscribed angle is half the arc
ways.when: Use this when the angle's vertex sits on the circle itself.
steps: A wheel's inscribed angle P looks at arc AB, which measures 96 degrees.
An inscribed angle has its vertex on the circle, with two chords as its sides.
It always measures half of the arc it looks at, no matter where the vertex sits.
96 divided by 2 is 48, so angle P measures 48 degrees.
ways.example: A circle's inscribed angle P looks at arc AB of 96 degrees. Find angle P.
ways.trap: Using the full arc measure as the angle instead of taking half.

ways.name: The tangent meets the radius at a right angle
ways.when: Use this to find a tangent-chord angle when a radius is drawn to the point of tangency.
steps: A tangent line touches a wheel at point T. Chord TC and radius OT are drawn.
A tangent line always meets the radius at the point of tangency at a right angle.
Angle OTC, between the radius and the chord, measures 35 degrees.
The tangent-chord angle and angle OTC share that 90 degree angle: 90 minus 35 is 55.
ways.example: A tangent touches a circle at T. Radius OT and chord TC form a 35 degree angle OTC. Find the tangent-chord angle at T.
ways.trap: Forgetting the radius meets the tangent at exactly 90 degrees and guessing the split instead.

ways.name: Add inside, subtract outside
ways.when: Use this to remember whether to add or subtract the two arcs at a crossing point.
steps: Chords AC and BD cross inside a circle. Arc AB is 55 degrees and arc CD is 85 degrees.
When the vertex is inside the circle, where two chords cross, add the two opposite arcs.
55 plus 85 is 140, and half of that is 70.
If the vertex were outside instead, subtract the two arcs and halve, rather than add.
ways.example: Chords AC and BD cross inside a circle. Arc AB is 55 degrees and arc CD is 85 degrees. Find the angle at the crossing point.
ways.trap: Adding when the vertex is actually outside the circle, where the arcs should be subtracted instead.
